headline: New law sets deadlines for the Bureau of Indian Affairs to review and approve mortgages and related documents on tribal trust land.
what_it_does: The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA) must tell lenders when it receives mortgage or right-of-way documents for tribal trust land, do a first review within 10 days, and approve or deny them within 20 or 30 days, depending on the type. It also sets response times for title status reports and requires notice when processing is delayed. Tribes and certain federal agencies get read-only access to a BIA land and accounting records system. The law also creates a Realty Ombudsman position at the BIA and asks the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to study putting mortgage documents into digital form.

who_it_affects.group: People seeking home mortgages on tribal trust land
who_it_affects.how: Their home and land mortgage paperwork must be reviewed by the BIA within set deadlines.
Business leasehold mortgages must also be processed by the BIA within set time limits.
They must be notified when the BIA receives their documents and told about any processing delays.
They get read-only access to the BIA's Trust Asset and Accounting Management System.
It must meet new review deadlines, follow notice rules, and add a Realty Ombudsman position.
It must report on digitizing documents to speed up mortgage processing on Indian land.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted May 4, 2026; the summary does not give separate start dates for specific requirements.
